subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & recommended next steps
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & recommended next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard from Acme:
- Primary goal: deploy a chat-based assistant for internal support workflows (ticket summarization, triage suggestions, and policy-aware replies).
- 95th-pct latency target: <= 250ms on query path for short interactions (<= 256 tokens).
- Quality priority: minimize hallucinations on policy/legal content; higher precision in factual extraction is more important than ultra-open creative responses.
- Budget: ~ $800–1,200 / 1M tokens (hosted baseline) but open to optimized dedicated pricing for predictable traffic.
- Data controls: must be able to run in Private (VPC) for PDE in Q4 if pilot succeeds.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) We’ll run a 2-week eval/pilot with a shortlist of 3 candidate models, using the prompt set we discussed (attached).
2) Redwood will supply a brief eval summary (benchmarks: latency, cost-per-token estimate, basic QA/regression checks) and recommended deployment config.
3) Joint success criteria: 95th-pct latency <= 250ms (hosted/dev instance), hallucination rate < 3% on our eval prompts, and cost in line with your budget or reducible via Dedicated.

I’ve attached the prompt set we used in the demo and a short template for the pilot. Below are the candidate models I recommend — rationale and tradeoffs in the detailed email that follows.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.json

Thanks — I’ll follow up with concrete benchmark numbers and a recommended shortlist by EOD tomorrow.

—
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa — thanks for the quick recap and for sending the prompt set. A couple of clarifying Qs before you run the pilot: 

1) For the latency target, are the numbers you expect for hosted endpoints or for a Dedicated deployment? Our infra team is worried about bursty traffic and cold-starts.
2) On hallucination testing: can you include a small set of red-team prompts (legal/policy edge cases) in the eval so we can see failure modes?
3) Cost: the ballpark I gave is for hosted pricing. If Dedicated can bring the cost-down materially for expected steady-state traffic, we’re open to that.

If you can include the benchmark Drive link and the eval summary in your next message, that’d be perfect. We’re aiming to kick a pilot in the week of 7/6 if timelines align.

Alex — great questions. Attached are the short eval summary and the Drive link with per-model artifacts. I also added a small red-team prompt file to the prompt set (legal_edge_cases.txt) and ran it through the same checks.

Files/Links attached: acme_eval_summary_v1.pdf, acme_prompt_set_v1.json
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-acme-benchmarks
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/001234567/overview

Recommended 3-model shortlist + rationale (quick summary):

1) Redwood-OPT-7b-Q4 (recommended baseline)
- Expected latency (hosted, p95, <=256 tokens): ~120–160ms
- Cost: lowest per-token cost for high concurrency; good operating point for prompt-heavy workloads
- Quality: strong extractive/fact recall with tuned system prompts; low hallucination footprint on our eval (observed ~2.1% on your legal_edge_cases set)
- When to pick: if you need the lowest latency and lowest cost while keeping acceptable factuality. Good candidate for hosted pilot and Dedicated later.

2) Llama-2-13b-Chat-8bit (balanced quality/latency)
- Expected latency (hosted, p95, <=256 tokens): ~220–280ms (hosted; Dedicated can lower this)
- Cost: moderate; higher than OPT-7b but often better at nuanced instruction-following and policy adherence
- Quality: better conversational consistency, fewer style regressions; hallucination rate ~1.8% on the eval set but occasional verbosity on policy text
- When to pick: if precision on nuanced policy interpretation is critical and you can accept slightly higher latency or move to Dedicated for tighter SLOs.

3) Falcon-40b-Instruct (quality-first, higher cost)
- Expected latency (hosted, p95, <=256 tokens): ~400–600ms (hosted), recommend Dedicated for production to meet latency targets
- Cost: materially higher; better for the hardest extraction/complex reasoning tasks
- Quality: best overall factuality on our tests (~0.9% hallucination), strongest at multi-step extraction and synthesis
- When to pick: if Acme prioritizes quality over cost/latency for initial rollout (e.g., curated tickets, legal responses). Consider a hybrid routing policy (quality tier for risky queries, OPT-7b for routine triage).

Tradeoffs & deployment recommendations:
- Pilot approach: run all three in parallel for 2 weeks using the attached prompt set and your live anonymized ticket samples. We’ll gather p95 latency, cost/user, hallucination rates, and subjective QA scores from your SME reviewers.
- Routing: we recommend starting with a single-model pilot (Redwood-OPT-7b-Q4) plus limited traffic routed to Falcon-40b for the legal prompts to measure differential quality. This minimizes cost while giving targeted quality signals.
- Dedicated vs Hosted: for immediate testing hosted endpoints are fine. If pilot shows heavy steady traffic or strict latency needs with burst tolerance, Dedicated capacity reduces p95 by ~25–40% and provides reserved throughput.

Next steps / ask from Acme:
- Confirm pilot kickoff date (you mentioned week of 7/6).
- Share 500 anonymized sample tickets (can be S3/GDrive link or we’ll provide a secure upload).
- Internal SME to review final eval (Priya ok to be the reviewer?).

I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff to walk through the pilot plan and expected observability. Let us know preferred times.
